channel.title: Latest alerts from washingtonpost.com
channel.description: An unofficial feed created by Derek Willis.

item.title: The cellphone security feature everyone should enable — and not worry about
item.description: Using biometrics doesn’t expose this data to your device’s makers, and it provides greatly enhanced protection, our analysis from personal tech writer Rob Pegoraro explains.

item.title: Former FBI officials charged with lying to Congress about Hunter Biden laptop inquiry
item.description: For years, Democrats and Republicans have debated about the significance of the laptop, with Republicans saying it was key evidence of deep corruption within the family of Joe Biden and Democrats saying it was simply fodder for Republican conspiracy theories.

item.title: Colleges need to evolve. Not all bachelor’s degrees should take four years.
item.description: Four-year programs don’t meet the needs of every student.

item.title: Justice Dept. seeks to block certification of Alaska Senate race if Republican incumbent narrowly loses
item.description: The lawsuit cited confusion over two similarly named candidates, including Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan.

item.title: Ukraine’s Starlink access still restricted, according to Ukrainian official in U.S., despite Trump’s avowal otherwise
item.description: President Donald Trump had said Elon Musk lifted restrictions on Ukraine’s access to the satellite network. But Denys Sienik, Ukraine’s chargé d’affaires in the U.S., said Friday that “speed restrictions remain in place.” Ukrainian soldiers also said Friday they were still experiencing disruptions.

item.title: Netanyahu orders broad West Bank military operation after Hamas attack leaves 2 Israeli soldiers dead, others wounded
item.description: The two Palestinian attackers were killed, the Israeli military said. The shooting comes days before Israeli elections, which have centered on the prime minister’s handling of security issues.

item.title: Ramaswamy ad. Elon Musk. Trump rallies. Zuckerberg clash. Melanoma vaccine. Biometrics. Netflix experiment. Catch up now.
item.description: Today’s seven most important and interesting stories.

item.title: Zuckerberg went to war with Meta's board of directors over pay and power, document shows
item.description: The tech billionaire wanted to lock in his absolute power over Meta even if he sold off stock, but directors at the the $1.7 trillion company said no, according to a filing released by Meta. The episode was triggered by the immense spending required for the company to compete in artificial intelligence.

item.title: Breakthrough vaccine for the deadliest skin cancer cut the risk of death or recurrence of melanoma by almost half
item.description: The vaccine is based on mRNA technology that helped end the coronavirus pandemic, Moderna and Merck announced Thursday.

item.title: Justice Department looks into whether Corey Lewandowski illegally profited from role as DHS adviser
item.description: A lawyer for the former top adviser to ex-Homeland Security Secretary Kristi L. Noem has denied any wrongdoing.

item.title: Why replacing Susan Collins would be so costly for Maine
item.description: Why replacing Susan Collins would be so costly for Maine

item.title: A new $724 million museum is a visually stunning train wreck, columnist Philip Kennicott writes
item.description: Decontextualization at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art has made a mess of one of this country’s great collections.

item.title: Calley Means, an ally of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., quits amid White House delays on food policies
item.description: Means, who resigned from the Trump administration, has been a key player in Kennedy’s food agenda and the Make America Healthy Again movement.

item.title: A remarkable picture is emerging of how the air around us could harm the brain
item.description: Pollution has long been indirectly linked with dementia. Now scientists wonder whether it could be physically reshaping the brain.

item.title: Hegseth wanted Eisenhower’s globe for his office. His staff broke it during a botched relocation attempt.
item.description: Photos obtained by The Post show a gash in the World War II-era artifact.

item.title: Virginia state Sen. L. Louise Lucas indicted as part of corruption probe involving family-run marijuana business
item.description: Lucas, the 82-year-old president pro tempore of the Virginia Senate, is one of the state’s most powerful Democrats.

item.title: Judge restricts Homeland Security investigations into noncitizen voters in nine states, citing flawed data
item.description: Heading into the midterm elections, the Department of Homeland Security has launched a wide-ranging effort to track down noncitizens it suspects of voting or registering to vote. A federal judge found the process was prone to errors that could sweep U.S. citizens into voter-fraud investigations.

item.title: Which states are the most free? A new report scores all 50.
item.description: The results don’t track neatly along political lines.

item.title: Netanyahu says U.S. and Israel must topple Iranian regime
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Iran posed an “existential threat” and that President Donald Trump had said he was “ready to finish the job.”

item.title: El-Sayed, Rogers clash in Michigan’s final Senate debate, lacing policy answers with personal jabs. See our takeaways.
item.description: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers are locked in a close race for the pivotal seat.

item.title: Here’s what to expect if you’re taking a month off from drinking
item.description: Pausing alcohol consumption, even for just a few weeks, can have noticeable benefits. Experts explain what Sober October or Dry January can and can’t do for your health.

item.title: Pentagon looks to build a deep-cover spy program to confront China
item.description: Economic espionage is a new priority at the Defense Department. But the Pentagon doesn’t have a great track record with human spying.

item.title: Medical tests show Pope Leo requires no further treatment for lung cancer
item.description: Pope Leo’s doctors have also said there is “no clinical reason” to stop him from continuing with his upcoming trip to Latin America next month.

item.title: The cascading absurdities of a downward-spiraling presidency
item.description: The cascading absurdities of a downward-spiraling presidency

item.title: Trump officials ask Supreme Court to let border security project resume in and around Big Bend National Park in Texas
item.description: The move comes after an injunction blocking construction on a more than 500-mile stretch of the project.

item.title: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion in New Mexico for misleading users on privacy
item.description: The judgment is one of the largest of its kind, according to the state’s attorney general, and exceeds an $18 billion child safety settlement Meta agreed to in August.

item.title: Cops who left the force kept covertly tracking people via a powerful camera network
item.description: Incidents of unauthorized access tallied by The Post reveal how easily users could gain or retain access to data from Flock’s vast network of roadside cameras.

item.title: U.S. gets its first new national park in six years
item.description: Arizona’s Chiricahua became the 64th national park late Tuesday when President Trump signed the Chiricahua National Park Act.

item.title: Supreme Court allows gender transition care for federal prisoners for now
item.description: The justices denied the government’s request to freeze a lower-court order that found the administration’s decision to end such care for prisoners was not backed by sufficient evidence. The lower court had ordered the treatment to continue.

item.title: Democrats sue Trump, Justice Dept. over effort to remove voters from state rolls ahead of midterms
item.description: The complaint alleges that Trump administration officials have directed threats and intimidation at state and local election officials.

item.title: The U.S. is pushing for Ukraine peace talks. Is Putin interested?
item.description: Steve Witkoff carries a peace plan to Russia, and the world will soon know who’s stalling.

item.title: A GOP attack ad featuring Democrat Amy Acton’s estranged mother has Ohio governor’s race in an uproar
item.description: Vivek Ramaswamy’s campaign said it would spend $4 million to air the ad, which shows Acton’s mother calling her daughter “a liar.” Acton was removed from her mother’s home when she was 12 after her stepfather was indicted on a charge of raping her.

item.title: Russia releases U.S. citizen Stephen Hubbard as envoy Steve Witkoff meets Vladimir Putin in St Petersburg
item.description: Hubbard was captured by Russian soldiers in eastern Ukraine in 2022, and later transferred to Russia. On Tuesday, President Donald Trump said he had been speaking to the Russian leader about his release.

item.title: How a photo of a patient’s face could predict whether they’ll survive cancer
item.description: Researchers say they’ve developed an AI model trained on more than 40 million photographs that can help predict mortality risk.

item.title: Here’s an idea: Don’t build a 250-foot obstacle near a risky airport
item.description: Compounding risk is how disasters happen.

item.title: Commanders star receiver Terry McLaurin out for rest of season with torn patellar tendon
item.description: McLaurin injured his left knee during the team’s Monday night loss to the 49ers. Coach Dan Quinn said Tuesday that he will need surgery.

item.title: Texas redistricting may backfire — and take out some rising Latino GOP stars
item.description: After the president pushed the state to redraw its congressional districts, the decisions made in South Texas are haunting Republicans.

item.title: A Maryland woman’s husband died in ICE custody. She wants answers.
item.description: More than two weeks after the death, agency officials have yet to provide the family with a detailed account of what happened, Veronica Ramirez said. She knew her husband, Julian Curo Churata, as a healthy 47-year-old with no history of health issues.

item.title: You may be frugal, but here are the few years when you should spend away, columnist Michelle Singletary writes
item.description: When you spend decades in saving mode, flipping a switch to spending mode can be very uncomfortable, our columnist writes. If you’re struggling to give yourself permission to spend in retirement, follow these steps.

item.title: From Ohio’s cornfields and factories comes a warning for Republicans
item.description: The working class is preparing to send a midterms message.

item.title: Small group of national security officials advises representatives from 10 states and both parties who fear Trump election meddling
item.description:
The group includes about 10 current and former officials with experience in the Defense Department, some of whom have previously focused on countering authoritarianism abroad.
Their efforts are motivated not by political bias, they say, but a growing sense of alarm that President Donald Trump will harm American democracy by undermining the integrity of the vote to keep the Republican Party in power.

item.title: Why anxiety can feel worse at night and what to do about it
item.description: Here’s why your mind tends to race right when you should be winding down for bed and how you can minimize the anxiety.

item.title: Supreme Court to hear case challenging admissions criteria for Maryland middle-school program
item.description: A group of parents contend the criteria to a selective magnet program in Montgomery County put Asian American students at a disadvantage.

item.title: Trump administration delays transfer of Patriot missiles meant for Ukraine
item.description: Delays in approving the transfers from partner countries coincide with a worsening rupture between President Donald Trump and Volodymyr Zelensky.

item.title: My sister may have visited me after death. Turns out there’s a term for it.
item.description: After my sister’s death, I found her again — in my yard.

item.title: The Maya collapse was blamed on drought. The full story is more complicated.
item.description: Researchers are still puzzling through what happened to the ancient civilization, which mysteriously dwindled. New answers have parallels in the present.

item.title: Ann Hornaday, longtime Washington Post film critic, dies at 66
item.description: The Pulitzer Prize finalist in criticism also wrote a book about how to watch movies. She brought a casual though knowledgeable approach to her reviews.
